result.topic_en: Euler shows that the residues of the powers of a recur in the same order once unity reappears, that a^{P-1} leaves remainder 1 when a is a primitive root, and states that an incomplete residue series has a number of terms that is an aliquot part of P-1.
result.transcription:
90 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
numerum primum P diuidi nequit, (radix enim $a$ diuisore P minor ideoque ad eum prima statuitur), necessario alter factor $a^{\nu}-1$ per P diuisionem admittet, hincque potestas $a^{\nu}$ per P diuisa vnitatem relinquet; quae potestas cum inferior sit quam $a^{\mu+\nu}$, euidens est, residuum $\varepsilon$ ante recurrere non posse, quam vnitas recurrerit.
20 Statim atque in serie residuorum $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ etc. vnitas iterum occurrit, deinceps eadem residua eodem ordine vti ab initio iterum recurrent.
Dem. Oriatur enim vnitas secunda vice ex potestate $a^{\nu}$ ac sequens residuum erit $\alpha$, $1\ (5) = a$, idem quod ex secundo termino $a$ nascebatur, ideoque $\alpha$, post quod denuo sequentur residua $\beta, \gamma, \delta$ etc. eodem ordine vti ab initio.
21. Si $a$ sit radix primitiua, eius potestas $a^{P-1}$ per diuisorem primum P diuisa vnitatem relinquet.
Dem. Quia $a$ est radix primitiua in serie residuorum omnes numeri diuisore P minores occurrunt, quorum multitudo est $P-1$; ex totidem ergo progressionis geometricae terminis $1, a^{1}, a^{2}, a^{3}$ etc. oriantur necesse est; quorum vltimus erit $a^{P-2}$; sequens ergo terminus $a^{P-1}$ aliquod ex residuis praecedentibus reproducet, quod autem necessario est vnitas (19).
22. Si progressio geometrica $1, a, a^{2}, a^{3}, a^{4}$ etc. seriem residuorum \textit{incompletam} producat; numerus residuorum diuersorum erit pars aliquota numeri $P-1$ hoc est diuisoris primi P vnitate minuti.
Dem.

items.quote: Statim atque in serie residuorum $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ etc. vnitas iterum occurrit, deinceps eadem residua eodem ordine vti ab initio iterum recurrent.
items.english: As soon as unity occurs again in the series of residues 1, α, β, γ, δ etc., thereafter the same residues will recur again in the same order as from the beginning.

items.quote: Si $a$ sit radix primitiua, eius potestas $a^{P-1}$ per diuisorem primum P diuisa vnitatem relinquet.
items.english: If a is a primitive root, its power a^{P-1} divided by the prime divisor P will leave unity.

items.quote: Si progressio geometrica $1, a, a^{2}, a^{3}, a^{4}$ etc. seriem residuorum \textit{incompletam} producat; numerus residuorum diuersorum erit pars aliquota numeri $P-1$ hoc est diuisoris primi P vnitate minuti.
items.english: If the geometric progression 1, a, a^2, a^3, a^4 etc. produces an incomplete series of residues, the number of distinct residues will be an aliquot part of the number P-1, that is, of the prime divisor P diminished by unity.
